workshops.title: Delivery lab: check artifact identity, changed evidence, and review
workshops.summary: Run a local evidence checker, introduce controlled mismatches, and revise a copied proposal. Keep missing installation, diagnostic, and independent-review evidence pending.

simple.story: A parcel desk writes a packing list and records a check value for the contents of one sealed box. Later, someone swaps one page inside the box but leaves its label and packing list unchanged. The desk recalculates the check value and spots the mismatch. The old record no longer describes these contents. Matching contents would still not prove who packed the box or whether the parcel is suitable for delivery. Those questions need their own evidence and review.
simple.meaning: An attachment hash binds the declared record to particular bytes. DeliveryLab reads the attachment and compares its digest with the recorded hash. A review fingerprint separately binds review to decision inputs. Neither check authenticates a claimed reviewer or proves an artifact's behavior.

example.before: A scratch copy of pending.json points to synthetic-result.txt. Its bytes match the declared sha256. Review is still proposed, so the starting record remains pending with exit status 2.
example.change: Change one byte in the copied attachment while leaving the record's sha256 unchanged, then validate that copied record against its scratch root.
example.after: The validator reports changed-evidence and exits 1 for invalid input. A matching filename, version, or revision label cannot restore agreement with the old hash.

picture.caption: Changing attachment bytes invalidates the evidence binding even when the labels stay the same.

items.label: Declared hash
items.text: The record names the attachment and stores its expected digest.

items.label: Bytes change
items.text: One byte changes while the record keeps its old digest.

items.label: Recompute

items.label: Reject drift

words.meaning: A retained output, such as a build product, test result bundle, trace, or report.
A digest calculated from bytes and used here to detect a changed attachment.
An image identifier used with architecture to match a binary image to its symbols.
Information that maps compiled addresses to useful function and source names.
A digest of the decision inputs that a review must match.
Required evidence or review is missing, so the relevant decision stays open.

simple.remember: A matching label is not matching evidence, and matching evidence still needs the right review.
simple.boundary: The parcel story explains drift, not trusted provenance. Hash checks cannot authenticate source revision, signatures, reviewer identity, or causality. The local gate does not sign, install, symbolicate, or approve production delivery. Device observations and independent organizational review require their own actual artifacts.

sections.title: Know what the local artifact checker does
sections.html:
An artifact is a retained output that supports a claim, such as a build product or diagnostic report. DeliveryLab checks whether supplied evidence records agree. It is a standard-library Python validator with synthetic JSON fixtures, negative tests, and a standalone Swift contract example. A negative test deliberately supplies a bad case and checks the reason for rejection. The validator reads local files and emits consistency results. It does not sign an app, upload a build, change a client, or record learner completion. Use synthetic inputs until an authorized scratch-target task supplies actual artifacts.

The tool requires Python 3.10 or later for pathlib containment checks. The companion examples use Swift 6 language mode and Foundation and run on the host with no iOS-only API. The recorded author verification used Python 3.14.5 and Apple Swift 6.4; consult the README for exact observations and commands rather than assuming those versions are required everywhere. Keep compilation, host execution, installed Apple command help, target interaction, device recording, and distribution evidence in separate rows.

Start from pending.json. Metadata means the fields describing the artifact. These fields agree with one another, but the fixture has no real independent review or manual artifact checks. wrong-identity.json changes environment and symbol UUID independently. changed-constraint.json keeps a widget exception visible. These fixtures are examples of records, not release records or organizational approvals.

sections.title: Run the checks and explain zero, invalid, and pending
sections.html:
An exit status tells you how the command finished. Record it together with the output rather than treating every nonzero status as the same failure. Run the README's unittest command with bytecode caches in your temporary directory. The tests create isolated roots under /private/tmp and check allowed paths, attachment hashes, image identity, stale evidence, review state, and removal rules. Compile DeliveryExamples.swift with explicit Swift 6 language mode and a unique module-cache path. Run the executable. Its preconditions and typed errors check synthetic values; they are not device measurements.

Invoke validate.py with a fixture path, --root pointing at DeliveryLab, and a selected mode. Exit zero means the supplied record is consistent within that scope; exit one means invalid metadata or unreadable/changed attachments; exit two means required evidence or review remains pending. The starting proposal therefore returns two even though its identity facts agree. The bad fixture returns one. Do not suppress nonzero statuses to make a course exercise look completed.

Installation mode additionally requires captured signed-install, upgrade, and privacy-review evidence and manual check fields. Diagnostic mode requires a selected captured diagnostic kind. Deprecation mode requires captured consumer and outcome evidence, valid owner/decision-right rows, and no unresolved adoption exception. A host-test fixture cannot satisfy those modes. Captured is a supplied claim about provenance, meaning where the evidence came from. An independent reviewer must still inspect the file with the owning tools.

sections.title: Change bytes or requirements and detect the stale record
sections.html:
A hash is a digest of bytes. It can detect a changed attachment, but does not certify that attachment's origin. Evidence paths are relative to the explicit root. The validator rejects absolute paths, parent traversal, symlink evidence, missing files, stale revisions, and changed hashes. For a directory, the digest includes sorted relative file names and each file's hash. A rename can therefore change the digest even if the file contents stay identical. This is useful for copied result bundles, where names and membership are part of the contract. It is a bounded consistency check, not protection against hostile filesystem races.

Copy a fixture into your own scratch directory and preserve the copied attachment layout. Change one byte of synthetic-result.txt while retaining the recorded hash. Validation must reject changed-evidence. Restore the bytes, then add a required localization to the record. The packaging requirement now fails unless the inventory includes it; even after inventory correction, an old review fingerprint must fail. Record which counterexample changes implementation and which changes only supplied evidence.

A review fingerprint is a digest of the inputs the reviewer evaluated. It covers all decision inputs except the review object. Review fields are excluded so attaching a review does not recursively invalidate itself. Evidence bytes are represented through their digests, which are checked independently. This cannot prove that a sourceRevision label identifies authentic source or that a reviewer label identifies a distinct person. Preserve original reports and actual host stdout, and have a human reviewer evaluate those limits.

sections.title: Get a real review, revise, and check the final inputs
sections.html:
An independent review is feedback from someone other than the author. Begin with a claim table: metadata is synthetic, local negative cases were executed, and device and organizational rows are pending. Ask a reviewer to inspect the candidate and try a counterexample. A useful finding identifies a mechanism, such as omitted architecture matching or acceptance of stale review. It also states what would show the issue is resolved. An invented reviewer string in a fixture is not participation. If no reviewer is available, keep that row pending while completing the local checks.

A blocking finding must be resolved before acceptance. An advisory finding may proceed under a documented decision. Record which category each reviewed finding belongs to. Revise the implementation or acceptance contract and explain the correction. Retest the changed revision and inspect the new result, then bind the reviewed fingerprint to its final inputs. An unresolved blocker cannot be closed by merely marking it accepted. An advisory issue can have a documented owner and reason. The local tests verify these structural rules; actual criticism and acceptance require the external review note.

For a future UI, say who owns execution and who handles a cancellation request. Synchronous hashing is eager and does not become background work merely because a task was created. Capture candidate/generation identity and reject late commits after navigation or replacement. Those UI schedules and representative bundle recordings remain target-required practice. Kotlin lifecycle scopes offer an ownership analogy, but Swift actor inheritance, structured task lifetime, and iOS extension processes have their own boundaries.

sections.title: Use actual files for diagnostic and installation claims
sections.html:
A diagnostic is a report or recording about an observed run. Each kind needs its own evidence. For an authorized scratch test run, preserve the .xcresult bundle and tool coordinates. Then run the README's installed xcresulttool test-results summary command against that path. For a trace, keep the complete recording, selected interval definition, and workload context. For a crash, keep the raw report and symbols with matching image UUID and architecture. UUID identifies the binary image; architecture identifies its instruction set. For jetsam, read the selected process and pageSize. A jetsam report is not an app thread backtrace.

The validator only checks evidence consistency and declared kind; it does not parse every Apple format, symbolicate, or prove causality. Do not relabel the synthetic text as captured or create a directory ending in .xcresult and call it real evidence. No raw trace, result bundle, device report, or signed installation was available during author verification. Command help was inspected, which is a tool capability check rather than a diagnostic result.

For manual installation, use a learner-owned scratch target with separately authorized signing or beta steps. Test fresh installation and a preserved-baseline upgrade separately, recording identity, environment, resources, permission states, account storage, and relevant extensions. Failed or cancelled tasks keep their rows open. Course authoring grants no production distribution authority, and a local gate pass supplies none.

sections.title: Keep the old reader while a widget still needs it
sections.html:
Deprecation tells future callers to move away from an interface. Removal ends support and needs stronger evidence. Run changed-constraint.json in deprecation mode. Its widget exception names an owner, reason, review date, and compensating check, but removal stays pending. The widget can read shared durable state when the app's process-local actor does not exist. Include it among the consumers whose adoption must be checked. Require the storage system's supported coordination and old/new-reader evidence. A dependency bump or source warning does not show those combinations working.

State who funds the work and who can accept or challenge the change, as well as how the architecture changes. Fund consumer integration and the temporary supported reader, give the widget owner authority to challenge compatibility, and name the service owner responsible for installed-client responses. Sequence compatible readers before new-format writers. Treat the exception date as a review trigger, and define what observation would close it. If a separate native adapter is required, retain shared external outcomes without pretending the implementations are identical.

Retest the revised evidence record and keep the decision conditional: a bounded app pilot may continue while widget adoption, device evidence, and removal remain pending. Source deprecation can guide future code before service retirement, but installed clients continue executing old binaries. Record actual outcome windows only when collected. No invented teams, adoption percentages, maintenance savings, or customer improvements should appear in the final report.

exercise.brief: Run the local evidence checks on scratch copies. Obtain real critique when available, revise and retest the inputs, then assess the widget compatibility constraint.
steps: Run the Python tests and Swift host checks with unique temporary caches and outputs. Save the actual stdout and exit status.
Validate all three fixtures. Explain which results are invalid and which are pending, keeping their original provenance labels.
In a copied fixture, change attachment bytes and make a review stale. Save the exact counterexamples the validator rejects.
Ask an independent reviewer to identify a blocking mechanism issue and how to show it is fixed. Keep review pending if no reviewer is available.
Revise and retest the current input. Evaluate the widget exception in deprecation mode.
Write separate evidence rows for host checks, target/device behavior, installation, diagnostics, and organizational review.
acceptance: Actual host output is separate from synthetic-result.txt
Wrong environment, mismatched symbols, and attachment drift are rejected
A new decision input invalidates stale review
Independent feedback is real or explicitly unavailable
Exception and missing captured evidence prevent removal
No signing, publication, client changes, measurements, or learner completion are implied
exercise.solution:
The starting proposal is pending because independent review and retest are incomplete. The bad fixture is invalid for two separate reasons: artifact.environment differs from the expected environment, and the arm64 symbol UUID differs from the binary image UUID. Matching one would not fix the other. In deprecation mode, the changed-constraint fixture is pending because the widget exception is unresolved and captured consumer/outcome evidence is missing. These are the expected outcomes of controlled examples. They show how the local decision rules work; they do not establish installation, diagnosis, adoption, or release approval.

A substantial revision uses the reviewer counterexample 'change required resources after approval.' Add a localization requirement to a copied record. The first failure is missing-resource. After inventory correction, the old reviewed fingerprint is stale, so review and retest must bind the final inputs. A complementary attachment-byte mutation produces changed-evidence even when version and sourceRevision strings remain unchanged. Preserve actual test stdout and a genuine review note; a synthetic peer label cannot replace either artifact.

When the reviewer adds shared widget storage, keep the old reader and assign widget/durable-data compatibility owners. The compensating task covers old/new reader-writer combinations, interruption, account separation, and protected-data states where relevant. The local ledger can check ownership completeness, but actual storage coordination and target interactions remain unverified. A review date requests reassessment instead of authorizing deletion.

The final decision accepts only bounded host consistency behavior supported by executed tests. If an independent person did not review, that gate remains pending. Actual crash symbolication, xcresult extraction, trace investigation, signed fresh installation/upgrade, consumer adoption, and operational recovery also remain pending until their own artifacts exist. List the next collector and required file for each gap. This report is a reviewable delivery artifact with explicit limits, never an automatic release or completion certificate.

quiz.question: The attachment hash matches. What still requires review?
options: Whether the supplied captured artifact is genuine and supports the claimed behavior
Whether file names exist in a string
quiz.explanation: Integrity checks detect drift. They do not authenticate provenance, parse every format, establish causality, or confirm human review.

quiz.question: A widget exception has a complete owner and date. What does the deprecation gate do?
options: Keep removal pending until compatibility and adoption criteria are satisfied
quiz.explanation: Complete exception metadata supports accountability. It does not close the exception or prove the old reader can be removed.

quiz.question: What is justified by these author checks?
options: Executed local contract checks and inspected command syntax, with device/organizational rows pending
quiz.explanation: The actual scope is host validation and tool discovery. No signing, real diagnostic extraction, device measurement, or organizational adoption was obtained.
